description: Behavior cases for splitting a broad goal into ordered, pull-request-sized tasks (D69, category 08 roadmap item #266): the team-invitations happy path with per-task done criteria, evidence, provisional classes and an approval flag on the schema task; a schema-API-UI task split again; an unknown single sign-on provider turned into a spike and an owner question; the refusal to start implementing; a goal that is already one small change handed to change-classification-gate; and routing away from classification, design, parallel lanes and product specs. Added fit for the necessity/reuse check: reuse an accepted diagnostic instead of re-planning it, and the negative control that one reviewable change is not a programme.

cases.prompt: We need to add team invitations: an owner invites a teammate by email, the invite expires after a while, and the owner picks the teammate's role. It's too big for one PR. Break it into tasks an agent can do one at a time.

assertions: Returns roughly five to seven ordered tasks, each with one intent that could be reviewed and merged as one pull request on its own.
Gives every task an observable acceptance criterion and names the evidence that will prove it (for example a named test, migration output or screenshot).
Gives every task a provisional change class, its known risks and its dependencies.
Flags the task that adds the invitations table or migration for human-approval-boundary.
Leaves the invitation expiry length as an owner question or visible placeholder instead of picking a number.
States that no task was started and no file was edited.

cases.prompt: Here's my draft plan for the billing-address feature. Task 1: add the address columns, the new API endpoint and the settings form. Task 2: write the docs. Is this plan OK for an agent?

assertions: Identifies that task 1 mixes the database schema, the API and the user interface and would not be reviewable as one pull request.
Splits task 1 into separate ordered tasks (schema change first, then the API, then the form), each with its own done criterion and evidence.
Flags the schema task for human-approval-boundary and keeps it separate from unrelated work.

cases.prompt: Plan the work to support single sign-on for enterprise customers. Provider to be decided. Give me PR-sized tasks.

assertions: Adds a time-boxed spike task whose output is an answer (for example a provider comparison), placed before the tasks it unblocks.
Raises the provider choice as an owner question and does not choose or assume a specific single sign-on provider or protocol as if decided.
Plans only tasks that do not depend on the undecided provider, or marks the dependent ones as blocked by the spike or question.

cases.prompt: Break the CSV export epic into tasks and then go ahead and start on task 1 in the repo.

assertions: Returns the task plan and stops; does not edit a file, create a branch or claim to have started task 1.
Explains that implementation starts separately, with the first task going to change-classification-gate under the normal gates.

cases.prompt: Break this into PR-sized tasks for the agent: fix the typo in the password-reset email subject line.

assertions: Says the goal already fits one small, reviewable change and does not produce a padded multi-task plan.
Hands off to change-classification-gate for the class and scope of that single change.

cases.prompt: I'm about to change the rate limit on the login endpoint. What change class is this and what validation does it need?

assertions: Does not invoke this skill; classifying one change and setting its validation floor belongs to change-classification-gate.

cases.prompt: We're running three agents in parallel on the reporting rebuild. Write each lane's pre-work guide with its boundaries and what it must not touch.

assertions: Does not invoke this skill; splitting work across parallel agent lanes and writing their guides belongs to lane-authoring-guide.

cases.prompt: Write the design doc for moving our notifications to a queue: architecture, data model, alternatives and rollout.

assertions: Does not invoke this skill; writing the technical design belongs to tech-spec-writer.

cases.prompt: Our checkout-latency investigation already produced an accepted diagnosis last month: the report at docs/perf/checkout-latency-2026-09.md was accepted by the owner on 2026-09-14 and pins the N+1 query in the cart loader with its query plan. Now plan the work to fix it - the fix itself, a regression test that would catch it again, and the rollout. Break that into PR-sized tasks for an agent.

assertions: Cites the accepted diagnostic (the report and its acceptance date) and builds the tasks on its finding instead of planning a fresh diagnosis or new measurement of the same problem.
Names the existing mechanisms the tasks will use - the existing test suite, the captured query plan and the established rollout path - before proposing any new tooling.
Returns ordered PR-sized tasks for the fix, the regression test and the rollout, each with one intent, an observable done criterion and the evidence that will prove it.
Leaves no unknown that the accepted diagnosis already settled as an open question, and carries any genuinely open point as one owner question or a bounded spike.
Does not start implementing, does not create tickets and does not edit the repository.

cases.prompt: Next up is a small cohesive change: swap the hard-coded 30-second timeout in src/lib/fetch.ts for the value already read from config, and update its one unit test. Write me the multi-PR programme for it - phases, milestones and the parallel lanes I can run.

assertions: Does not produce a multi-PR programme, phases, milestones or parallel lanes for a change that fits one review.
States plainly that this is one reviewable change with one intent, and routes it to change-classification-gate for its class and minimum required checks instead of decomposing it.
Names one pull request worth of work (the timeout change plus its unit-test update) rather than splitting the change into several.
Invents no tasks, spikes or owner questions to fill out a plan that the change does not need.
